review.shorterRoute: Native wpNormZ already has the exact integral-matrix transformation, holomorphy, bounds at infinity for every nonzero torsion index, and Fourier coefficients. Construct only the weight-two Gamma1 form 12*wpNormZ at (0,c), using these native proofs and the native all-cusp criterion. Then apply the finite Fourier transform to obtain integral forms whose combinations recover the two toric invariants. Defer general Tate uniformization, non-toric slots and arbitrary-curve naturality; the eventual finite-fiber application needs the generic ofJ curve with its full-torsion field. The native qExpansionAddHom and SlashAction.sum_slash replace further finite-sum inductions. The Tate a4 coefficient series alone suffices for the quadratic invariant; Tate a6, ellipticity, non-toric slots and uniformization are deferred to the exact-order point obligation. The actual B and D forms, integer coefficients, exact Gamma0 action and literal Laurent identities are assembled without certificates.
assumptionsToDischarge: Actual weight-two Gamma1 torsion modularity, holomorphy and all-cusp bounds are derived from native Weierstrass theorems.
Exact width-one Fourier coefficients are obtained from native width conversion and finite exponent fibers, then finite divisor sums.
Level-squared and level-fourth finite Fourier combinations construct actual weight-two B and weight-four D modular forms with explicit integer coefficients.

The actual Gamma0 slash action is the dual index permutation by the upper-left entry; literal Laurent identities reconstruct both toric invariant series in every coefficient field admitting the prescribed primitive root.
